title: Court sets Nov 23 for Facebook lawsuits
desc: A legal battle brought by the Thailand Consumers Council against businesses allegedly involved in online scams conducted through Facebook has moved forward, with the Bangkok South Civil Court scheduling the next hearing for Nov 23.
title_cn: 曼谷法院定于11月23日开庭审理Facebook诈骗案
summary_cn: 泰国消费者协会对涉嫌通过Facebook进行网络诈骗的商家提起的诉讼案件取得进展，曼谷南民事法院已将下次庭审日期定为2026年11月23日。该案涉及在线购物平台的诈骗防范责任，对在泰侨民和外籍人士的网络消费安全具有重要警示意义。建议在进行线上交易时提高警惕，核实卖家身份和产品真伪。
desc_original: A legal battle brought by the Thailand Consumers Council against businesses allegedly involved in online scams conducted through Facebook has moved forward, with the Bangkok South Civil Court scheduling the next hearing for Nov 23.

title: Dual nationality issues set for talks
desc: Thailand will seek Malaysia's cooperation in addressing long-standing problems involving dual nationals along the border amid concerns over its potential security implications in the southern border provinces, National Security Council (NSC) secretary-general Chatchai Bangchuad said on Tuesday.
title_cn: 双重国籍问题将启动双边会谈
summary_cn: 泰国国家安全委员会秘书长将与马来西亚磋商，解决边界沿线长期存在的双重国籍问题。该问题涉及南部边境省份的安全隐患，需要两国合作应对。
desc_original: Thailand will seek Malaysia's cooperation in addressing long-standing problems involving dual nationals along the border amid concerns over its potential security implications in the southern border provinces, National Security Council (NSC) secretary-general Chatchai Bangchuad said on Tuesday.

title: Sex workers urge PM to back rights bill
desc: Sex worker rights groups on Tuesday urged Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul to endorse a citizen-sponsored bill seeking legal protection and labour rights for sex workers.
title_cn: 性工作者权益组织敦促总理支持《权益法案》
summary_cn: 性工作者权益倡导组织呼吁总理阿努廷支持公民提议的法案，旨在为性工作者争取法律保护和劳动权益。这是推进泰国性工作者权益保障的重要举措。
desc_original: Sex worker rights groups on Tuesday urged Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul to endorse a citizen-sponsored bill seeking legal protection and labour rights for sex workers.

title: Govt boosts flood-response funds
desc: Deputy prime ministers will each receive 100 million baht in emergency funding to tackle flooding and prepare for drought across the nation.
title_cn: 政府增加洪灾应急资金
summary_cn: 泰国政府为每位副总理拨款1亿泰铢作为紧急资金，用于全国各地防洪和应对干旱。此举旨在强化灾害应对能力，保护人民生命财产安全。
desc_original: Deputy prime ministers will each receive 100 million baht in emergency funding to tackle flooding and prepare for drought across the nation.

title: Cabinet approves 7-point school safety plan
desc: The cabinet on Tuesday approved seven urgent measures to strengthen safety at schools nationwide following last week's shooting at Debsirin Nonthaburi School, including screening for weapons, illegal items and drugs before anyone enters school premises.
title_cn: 内阁批准七点校园安全计划
summary_cn: 继德布西林农乐校枪击事件后，泰国内阁批准七项校园安全措施，包括进校前的武器、违禁品和毒品检查。该计划旨在强化全国学校安保，防止类似悲剧再次发生。
desc_original: The cabinet on Tuesday approved seven urgent measures to strengthen safety at schools nationwide following last week's shooting at Debsirin Nonthaburi School, including screening for weapons, illegal items and drugs before anyone enters school premises.

title: Cabinet backs civil service overhaul to rein in personnel costs
desc: The cabinet on Tuesday approved a civil service reform programme aimed at reducing the public-sector workforce by 15% by 2032.
title_cn: 内阁批准公务员制度改革以控制人员成本
summary_cn: 泰国政府批准公务员改革计划，目标是到2032年将公共部门人力削减15%。这一改革旨在提高政府效率，控制人事成本，但也可能影响公共服务的运作。
desc_original: The cabinet on Tuesday approved a civil service reform programme aimed at reducing the public-sector workforce by 15% by 2032.

title: BAAC chief faces backlash from staff
desc: Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas is set to convene an urgent board meeting over employee protests demanding the resignation of Chatchai Sirilai, president of the Bank for Agriculture and Agricultural Cooperatives (BAAC).
title_cn: 农业合作银行行长面临员工抗议
summary_cn: 泰国财政部长埃克尼替·尼提瑞（Ekniti Nitithanprapas）计划召集农业合作社银行（BAAC）紧急董事会会议。该行员工因不满行长察差·西里莱（Chatchai Sirilai）的管理，发动大规模抗议并要求其辞职。此事反映出管理层与员工之间的严重矛盾，财政部的介入表明事态严重性。
desc_original: Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas is set to convene an urgent board meeting over employee protests demanding the resignation of Chatchai Sirilai, president of the Bank for Agriculture and Agricultural Cooperatives (BAAC).

title: Cabinet backs wider milk access

title: Conservation activist Psi Samut calls for foreign workers to learn Thai
desc: Conservation activist Psi Samut calls for foreign workers to learn Thai Legacy Conservation activist Siranudh “Psi” Samutt criticised foreign workers in Thailand, arguing that those working in the country should make an effort to speak Thai , prompting widespread agreement from Thai social media users. Psi shared his views about foreign employees using English in Thailand on his X account, @Psisamutt , on Saturday, August 8. In the post, Psi said he usually responds in Thai when foreign employees at restaurants speak English to him. He said that if they cannot take his order in Thai, he asks to speak with a Thai employee instead. “I’m in Thailand, and I prefer to speak Thai,” Psi wrote, adding that he considered foreign workers who work in Thailand without being able to speak Thai to be taking advantage of the country. Photo via X/ @psisamutt Psi also argued that Thai people working overseas are expected to develop language skills because countries such as Japan and the US have strong cultures and global influence. The activist further criticised business operators who he said chose to reduce costs by hiring migrant workers , despite the minimum wage for Thai workers not being high

title: Anutin says shooting burglar at home still breaks Thai law
desc: Anutin says shooting burglar at home still breaks Thai law Legacy Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said today, August 11, that gun owners could still be breaking the law if they shot a burglar inside their own home, as he outlined plans for stricter gun laws across Thailand . Speaking at Government House, Anutin said the government was accelerating work on a new firearms law and had ordered relevant agencies to temporarily stop renewing three types of firearm licences, Por 3, Por 4 and Por 12, until the Cabinet decides otherwise. Anutin said officials would increase checkpoints focusing on firearms and drugs, adding that several cases had already been detected the previous night. He said police would oppose bail for people caught carrying firearms during the crackdown. title: Chiang Mai among 12 provinces facing heavy rain, flood risk
desc: Chiang Mai among 12 provinces facing heavy rain, flood risk Legacy Thailand is closely monitoring flood risks in 12 provinces , including Chiang Mai, as continued heavy rain raises the risk of flash floods , forest runoff and overflowing waterways, particularly in the north and northeast. The Royal Irrigation Department (RID) said today, August 11, that officials have been instructed to monitor conditions and prepare machinery, water pumps and personnel to assist residents in areas at risk. The 12 provinces under heightened surveillance are Chiang Rai, Chiang Mai, Mae Hong Son, Nan, Mukdahan, Saraburi, Roi Et, Yasothon, Nakhon Phanom, Udon Thani, Phitsanulok and Amnat Charoen. Thailand continues to experience heavy rain in some areas as a monsoon trough passes across the upper north and northern Laos. A relatively strong southwest monsoon is also covering the Andaman Sea, Thailand and the Gulf of Thailand. The conditions could bring heavy to very heavy rain and accumulated rainfall, increasing the risk of flash floods, forest runoff and overflowing waterways. Hillside areas, communities near waterways and low-lying areas face particular risks. Photo from Marc Mintel via Unsplash Th

desc: Former MP gunman fined for smoking in police custody Legacy Thailand’s Department of Disease Control (DDC) has fined former Nonthaburi MP Chalong Riewraeng 5,000 baht for smoking inside Rattanathibet Police Station, while the station itself was fined 3,000 baht for allowing the violation . DDC officials visited the station today, August 11, after images emerged of Chalong smoking inside a meeting room while in police custody. Officials said the station is a government building and therefore a smoke-free area under the Tobacco Products Control Act of 2017. A DDC public health official said photographs published in news reports provided clear evidence of the offence and were used to proceed under Section 42 of the law. Officials can issue fines when they discover a violation or receive a report.
